rows.o_value: NBS Microdata Catalog operating: 107 studies (checked 22 Aug 2026), including NASC 2022 agricultural census microdata (30,546 EAs; 767/774 LGAs; DDI/XML/JSON metadata; 5,342 downloads) and NASS 2023 with public-use files

rows.gate: The indicator name conjoins three qualifiers — open, machine-readable, AI-ready. The retrieved evidence supports only part of that. MACHINE-READABLE: the NBS catalogue study pages offer structured metadata in 'DDI/XML' and 'JSON' and anonymised microdata files, which is machine-readable metadata at minimum. OPEN: the catalogue header on every retrieved page reads 'NBS Website | Register | Login' and access is via a 'GET MICRODATA' request flow; the catalogue's own License search facet carries no stated licence in the retrieved text, so the datasets are registration-gated public-use files rather than openly licensed open data. AI-READY: nothing in the retrieved Nigeria pages evidences bulk/API delivery, versioned pipelines, harmonised machine-readable data dictionaries or a machine-readable licence — the only AI-readiness criteria in the sources come from a NOAA (United States) presentation, which is not evidence about Nigeria and was not applied to any Nigerian dataset. No Nigerian general open-data portal (e.g. a national data.gov catalogue) page was supplied, so the 'open portal' side of the census's open question could not be tested. The evidence therefore sits on the statistical-microdata side of the unresolved definition, not on the open/AI-ready side.

question_4.construct_note: The indicator names RURAL mobile broadband coverage. The best T1 evidence in the supplied pages is national: ITU's Nigeria dashboard reports population covered by at least a 3G mobile network (2022) at 87% and population covered by at least a 4G mobile network (2022) at 81%, plus mobile-cellular network coverage of 94%. These are whole-population figures with no urban/rural split, so they cannot stand in for rural coverage — in Nigeria the coverage gap is concentrated precisely in rural and remote LGAs, so a national figure will overstate the rural value by an unknown margin. The one rural-disaggregated ITU figure visible on that page is a different indicator entirely: households with Internet access at home, rural (2017) 2%. On the unratified definitional question flagged in the indicator census: this row should be judged against RURAL as named, which means the Egypt-style national at-least-3G number is not admissible here; ITU does publish 'Population covered by a mobile-cellular and a mobile-broadband network, total and by urban/rural area' as a global/regional time series (per the ITU Statistics page), but that is an aggregate release, not a Nigeria country value, and no Nigeria rural cell appears in any supplied page.
